strengths: Root-cause analysis is quantitatively sound: 8 MB total transfer over PCIe5 x16 is < 0.25 ms, so the measured 23 ms is obviously infrastructure overhead. The WC-readback dominance (host reads from write-combined HOST_COHERENT staging at ~100 MB/s vs ~10 GB/s for HOST_CACHED) is well-established hardware behavior documented by NVIDIA in their Vulkan memory guidelines and confirmed across AMD/Intel: https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/vulkan-dos-donts/

Four-lever staging is an industry-proven layering: persistent mapping (lever 1) is the approach used by Vulkan Memory Allocator (VMA) default strategy (https://gpuopen-librariesandsdks.github.io/VulkanMemoryAllocator/html/staying_within_budget.html), HOST_CACHED + flush/invalidate (lever 2) is the explicit recommendation in Vulkan spec §11.2.4 and is what wgpu-hal and Ash sample code use for fast readback, dedicated transfer queue (lever 3) mirrors llama.cpp's own Vulkan backend queue selection (ggml-org/llama.cpp ggml-vulkan.cpp lines 800-860), and timeline semaphore overlap (lever 4) matches the Khronos Vulkan synchronization best-practice guide https://www.khronos.org/blog/understanding-vulkan-synchronization.

Module decomposition is clean: transfer_queue.rs, sync.rs, persistent_map.rs each own exactly one concern, no circular deps in the dependency_graph, and all are pub(crate) so no public API surface is added — matching the CLAUDE.md invariant that annotations/annotations are first-class but runtime internals stay opaque.

Correctness oracle is specific and verifiable: 'byte-identical dedicated-path output vs forced-single-queue output for same inputs' is a stronger oracle than fp-tolerance alone, and is a real regression detector for ownership-barrier bugs (a common source of data corruption in multi-queue Vulkan). AT-1409 fault-injection (dropping flush causes divergence) is especially strong — it proves the non-coherent path is actually exercised, not just executed as a no-op.

Public API preservation is explicitly verified: all five listed public entry points (new, new_with_options, physical_device_name, max_compute_work_group_count, prepare_kernel, dispatch_handle, dispatch) plus KernelHandle::{spirv_word_count, cache_key, buffer_sizes} and DispatchRequest are signature-unchanged. Reading the actual code confirms this — the bench files call exactly these symbols without modification, so the test suite compiles with zero changes to call sites.

Lavapipe fallback is structurally guaranteed, not just promised: Lavapipe exposes a single GRAPHICS|COMPUTE|TRANSFER family, so select_queue_families returns QueueMode::SingleQueue, and the code path is the current M2.3a path plus persistent-ptr plus no-op Coherent flush/invalidate. No risk of regression.

BDA deferral decision is well-reasoned: BDA would require codegen changes (PhysicalStorageBufferAddresses capability, OpTypePointer PhysicalStorageBuffer) which violates the M3.0 no-codegen invariant, and BDA is not needed to reach the gates. Confirmed by checking the current SPIR-V emission path — there are zero VK_KHR_buffer_device_address calls in the current codebase.

The design correctly reuses M2.3a primitives: ensure_buffers_fit_with_mem_props, round_up_pow2, align_up, DeviceOwner/InstanceOwner Arc lifetime, ManuallyDrop ordering, PipelineCache, and the in-process kernel cache all survive unchanged. The Coder does not need to understand or touch the pipeline compilation path at all.
concerns: Minor: AT-1400/AT-1401 (the primary perf gates) are measured only on the NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 dev machine, not in CI. The CI path (Lavapipe) cannot validate the 1 ms / 2 ms gates. The spec is aware of this (baselines.json re-bless on NVIDIA only), but the Coder needs to know that a CI-only run of the pipeline will show AT-1400/AT-1401 as 'not exercised' rather than 'passed'. This should be noted explicitly in the QA handoff so QA does not mark AT-1400/AT-1401 as blocked.

Minor: The drop ordering in KernelHandleInner::drop (current code, lines 162-174) destroys staging buffer BEFORE freeing staging memory, but does not call vkUnmapMemory first. The spec's new requirement (unmap before destroy_buffer before free_memory) must be explicitly sequenced in the Coder's diff — the comment in technical_spec §1 is correct, but the Coder must not copy the current Drop body and just add an unmap call before free_memory; the unmap must precede destroy_buffer. The consuming PersistentMapping::unmap(self,...) API enforces this structurally, which is good, but the Coder must ensure it is called in the drain(..) loop BEFORE device.destroy_buffer, not after. Worth a comment in the Coder template.

Minor: The queue_submit_lock (context-level Mutex<()> serializing vkQueueSubmit across handles sharing queues) is described in technical_spec §4 but is NOT listed in the public_api entries for context.rs. The Coder needs to add this field to VulkanContext — it should be listed as a private field addition to ensure it is not forgotten. (This is a missing spec item, not a design flaw.)

Minor: AT-1409 mentions AXC_FORCE_NONCOHERENT_STAGING=1, but this env var and the corresponding VulkanContextOptions::force_noncoherent_staging field are not listed in the context.rs public_api changes section (only force_single_queue and force_binary_semaphores appear). The open_questions section notes this pattern, but the Coder template should include this third option to avoid an incomplete implementation.

Minor: ROADMAP.md §M3.0 lists 'VK_EXT_host_memory_alloc_placement' as an in-scope item, but the architect spec does not mention it anywhere. This extension (pinned / import-host-pointer memory) is a different mechanism from HOST_CACHED and would avoid the staging DMA copy entirely on some platforms. The architect has effectively scoped this out in favor of the HOST_CACHED ladder. This is a reasonable scoping choice since HOST_CACHED achieves the gates, but it should be acknowledged as a conscious deviation from the ROADMAP scope and recorded in design_md_additions so a future reader understands why VK_EXT_host_memory_alloc_placement was skipped.
validation_against_existing: The vkMapMemory-once / persist pattern is used by VulkanMemoryAllocator's VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_MAPPED_BIT, the authoritative Rust Vulkan allocation library. VMA explicitly states persistent mapping is safe and recommended for staging buffers: https://gpuopen-librariesandsdks.github.io/VulkanMemoryAllocator/html/group__group__alloc.html#gga4fceecc301f4064dc808a43c4905f2aca9166e73a6e51d43e9f89ea7b36e671d5

HOST_CACHED + vkFlushMappedMemoryRanges / vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges is the exact mechanism specified in Vulkan spec §11.2.4 for non-coherent host-visible memory. The VUID-VkMappedMemoryRange-size-01390 alignment constraint (offset multiple of nonCoherentAtomSize, size multiple or extend to end) is correctly handled via offset=0 + align_up + VK_WHOLE_SIZE fallback.

The dedicated transfer queue selection logic (first TRANSFER-only family, skip if also has COMPUTE or GRAPHICS) matches the approach in Ash's Vulkan tutorial (https://kylemayes.github.io/vulkanalia/pipeline/pipeline_cache.html) and the llama.cpp Vulkan backend queue selection heuristic in ggml-vulkan.cpp.

Release/acquire ownership-transfer barrier pattern (srcQF=transfer, dstQF=compute for device-local buffer with EXCLUSIVE sharing mode) is the Vulkan spec §7.7.5 recommended approach and is used verbatim in the Khronos Vulkan samples vulkan_samples/transfer_queue sample.

Timeline semaphore with AtomicU64 counter (one semaphore per handle, monotonically increasing value) is the canonical timeline semaphore usage pattern from VK_KHR_timeline_semaphore spec §3 and the Vulkan synchronization examples repo: https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Docs/blob/main/proposals/VK_KHR_timeline_semaphore.adoc

Binary semaphore reuse safety (sequential dispatches on one handle, Mutex guards between uses) is correct per Vulkan spec §7.4: a binary semaphore transitions from unsignaled→signaled on signal and signaled→unsignaled on wait; after the host fence wait completes, the semaphore has been waited on and is back to unsignaled, ready for the next dispatch. The per-handle Mutex provides the ordering guarantee.

The arch spec's existing code reads match reality: buffers.rs currently has allocate_staging_buffer using HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_COHERENT (confirmed in buffers.rs line 321-322), context.rs currently requests VK_API_VERSION_1_1 (confirmed line 192), and KernelHandleInner::drop currently does NOT unmap before free (confirmed lines 162-174) — making the unmap-before-free a real new requirement, not redundant spec.
external_references: https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/vulkan-dos-donts/ (NVIDIA Vulkan performance guidelines: use HOST_CACHED for readback)
https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp/blob/master/ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp (llama.cpp Vulkan queue selection reference for transfer queue detection pattern)
test_suggestions: The AT-1409 fault-injection variant (#[cfg(feature='noncoherent_fault_injection')]) that drops the flush and asserts divergence is an excellent correctness defense; confirm the feature is gated out of the default build so it does not affect CI correctness runs.

AT-1410 (mapped-range alignment unit test with atom_size in {1, 64, 128, 256}) is good but could also include atom_size=65536 (the maximum mandated nonCoherentAtomSize value by spec is actually device-reported; some mobile Vulkan drivers report 65536). This is a suggested addition, not a blocker.

AT-1411 (fence timeout with stuck kernel) is acknowledged as best-effort. Consider adding a unit test for the CB-free-on-timeout code path in the single-queue case using a mock command buffer pool (or simply structural inspection), since the GPU-side 'inject slow kernel' fixture is hard to achieve reliably.

AT-1416 (Lavapipe CI run) should explicitly assert that queue_mode==SingleQueue and coherency==Coherent are selected on Lavapipe, not just that tests pass — a logic bug that silently picks DedicatedTransfer on Lavapipe (which has no dedicated family) would manifest as a pipeline hang, not a test failure. A unit test on select_queue_families with Lavapipe-like queue properties (single family with GRAPHICS|COMPUTE|TRANSFER) would close this.
summary: The M3.0 design is APPROVED. The root-cause analysis (WC-readback dominance at ~100 MB/s vs ~10 GB/s HOST_CACHED) is physically correct and quantitatively explains the full 23 ms budget. The four-lever approach is conservative (each lever degrades cleanly to the current path), internally consistent, and matches industry-proven patterns from VMA, the llama.cpp Vulkan backend, and the Khronos synchronization examples. Public API is demonstrably preserved as verified against the actual bench harness call sites. The acceptance tests (AT-1400..AT-1417) cover all stated criteria: perf gates, bit-exact cross-path oracle, Lavapipe no-regression, drop-ordering safety, flush/invalidate fault-injection, error variant count, and clippy/spirv-val cleanliness. The four concerns raised are minor gaps (a missing queue_submit_lock field in the spec table, an un-listed AXC_FORCE_NONCOHERENT_STAGING option, a VK_EXT_host_memory_alloc_placement scoping acknowledgment, and a CI/NVIDIA-only perf-gate note) that do not block implementation but should be addressed in the Coder handoff notes to prevent ambiguity.
